title: LodeCore / Redwood partner orientation - technical & GTM discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery call to map technical integration options for LodeCore's edge accelerator appliances with Redwood's private and dedicated offerings. Covered deployment models (hosted vs dedicated vs on-prem/VPC), typical workloads (low-latency inference at edge for retail kiosks and robotics), security/compliance asks, and pilot next steps including benchmark plan and integration guide delivery.
action_items: Jordan Hayes - Share LodeCore partner integration one-pager and sample NGINX/proxy config - 2028-06-20
Priya Menon - Draft benchmark plan (latency P50/P95, throughput, quant profiles) and test dataset - 2028-06-24
Ellen Cho - Provide hardware spec sheet and sample workload manifests (k8s or bare-metal) - 2028-06-18
next_steps: Jordan to email partner integration guide + security checklist
Schedule 1-week pilot to run 10k inference tokens across 3 appliance units (date options: Jun 27-29)
Set up joint Slack channel and access to Redwood sandbox tenant for LodeCore engineers
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2028-06-15 14:30 UTC | Duration: ~46 minutes | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood Solutions), Marco Ruiz (LodeCore Head of Partnerships), Ellen Cho (LodeCore Director of Integrations), Samir Patel (LodeCore Lead DevOps), Rita Gomez (LodeCore Security Lead)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Intro call to align on technical onramp for LodeCore edge accelerators. Discussed integration patterns for private and dedicated, security needs (KMS/HSM, SSO), benchmark plan, and next steps to pilot.

00:00 Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account — with me Priya who's our SE and Aisha on solutions. How are you folks doing?
00:07 Marco Ruiz: Good. Thanks Jordan. Excited to chat, we've been following Redwood's stuff for a while.
00:11 Priya Menon: Awesome. Today we want to understand LodeCore's edge appliance footprint, common workloads, and what success looks like so we can propose the right onramp — hosted vs dedicated vs private.
00:22 Ellen Cho: Quick context, we build the LodeCore Edge-64 appliance, customers use it for low-latency inference in stores and for robotics. We want to offer an integrated path where Redwood can be an official serving runtime on our appliances and also surface it through our reseller channel.
00:35 Samir Patel: And we need to know what the pre-reqs are — kernel modules, driver versions, k8s or bare-metal support, that kind of thing.
00:42 Priya Menon: Great. On the Redwood side the runtime supports bare-metal installs and a lightweight k8s operator. We also have a private deployment mode that runs in the customer's VPC and a dedicated variant that can be reserved capacity in our infra. For edge appliances often bare-metal or k8s operator works best.
00:58 Rita Gomez: Security first thing — we need to understand encryption at rest, KMS/HSM options, audit logs, SOC2, and SSO support.
01:06 Jordan Hayes: Totally. We have SOC2 and, depending on the packaging, KMS integrations with AWS KMS and customer HSMs for private deployments. We'll send our security checklist.
01:14 Ellen Cho: When you say private packaging — is that a full control plane on our side or a split control plane? 
01:20 Priya Menon: It can be either. For VPC deployments we do a split control plane: customer manages data plane (serving) in their network, and Redwood can optionally host a control plane endpoint for orchestration. For fully air-gapped we provide an on-prem bundle. Note: sometimes the transcript here will garble 'control plane' as 'control plain' or similar.
01:36 Marco Ruiz: For the channel motion we want minimal friction. Can your runtime run with our provisioning tools? We have an installer and a management console.
01:43 Aisha Khan: We have a thin agent and operator that integrates with most installers; sample manifests and an Ansible playbook exist. We can map to your provisioning flow.
01:53 Samir Patel: How about model formats and quantization? Our customers push everything from full fp16 to 4-bit int8-ish stuff — we use a bunch of proprietary optimizations.
02:04 Priya Menon: We support standard ONNX and PyTorch formats, plus we do quantization-aware kernels. We also have recommended quant profiles; for edge units we often suggest 8-bit quant for throughput, but we do per-model quality checks. We'll want to run a small eval set during the pilot.
02:19 Samir Patel: Is the runtime compiled per-arch? We have AMD Instinct on some fleet and NVidia on others, and some of our new units are Arm-based.
02:27 Priya Menon: Yes — the runtime selects kernels by architecture, sequence length, and model shape. We do kernel selection at deploy time and can build optimized kernels for Arm on request. There was a small hiccup in the transcript where "kernel" came out as "car-nel".
02:39 Marco Ruiz: Latency numbers? We're targeting ~30-50ms p50 for small chat-like prompts on the kiosk use-case.
02:45 Priya Menon: That should be achievable on LodeCore Edge-64 with a tuned quant profile and prefix KV cache. For very tight p95 SLAs we often suggest local caching of embeddings or warm contexts. We'll propose a benchmark matrix.
02:58 Jordan Hayes: And to preview commercial, we often run a pilot where Redwood provides a trial license for the private bundle and we measure latency/cost. Channel resellers can co-sell — we can share margin/partner terms later.
03:10 Ellen Cho: Good. On security, Rita: our auditors need proof of key rotation, audit log retention, and SSO/SAML integration.
03:18 Rita Gomez: Also we need to know how logs are redacted and whether raw prompts can be prevented from leaving the appliance.
03:24 Priya Menon: For private/on-prem we never send raw prompts to Redwood unless customer opts in. Audit logs can be configured to redact PII, and we support SSO via SAML or OIDC, and KMS hooks to external HSMs. We'll include the security whitepaper.
03:39 Marco Ruiz: Integration level: do we need persistent internet? Some sites are intermittent.
03:44 Priya Menon: Intermittent connectivity is fine for local-only serving; for control plane sync and telemetry you'd want occasional bursts. For fully disconnected we have an offline bundle but that means no centralized telemetry and manual rollouts.
03:55 Samir Patel: Regarding telemetry — what metrics do you export? Prometheus?
03:59 Priya Menon: Prometheus metrics, token-level latency, per-model cost breakdowns, and traces we can forward to Jaeger or send to your observability pipeline.
04:10 Jordan Hayes: I want to call out one common tradeoff: dedicated hosted endpoints are easiest to manage but cost more; private on-prem gives best data control but requires more integration. For LodeCore's channel, maybe a hybrid where small customers get a hosted endpoint and larger customers get a private appliance bundle.
04:26 Marco Ruiz: That aligns with our go-to-market thinking.
04:29 Samir Patel: A couple of technical clarifications: 1) are there any kernel upgrades to the OS to support GPU drivers? 2) how do you handle KV cache eviction?
04:38 Priya Menon: 1) We list supported driver versions and kernel thresholds in the install doc — most customers run 5.15+ kernels for our drivers. 2) KV cache eviction is LRU-based with tunable bucket sizes; in transcripts sometimes 'LRU' is miswritten as 'L-R-U' or 'loo'.
04:55 Ellen Cho: Do you have an SDK or API we can wrap in our management console?
04:59 Jordan Hayes: Yes — REST + gRPC endpoints, plus a lightweight Node and Python SDK. We'll share example code.
05:06 Rita Gomez: About compliance, do you have a SOC2 letter and penetration test results?
05:10 Jordan Hayes: We have SOC2 Type II and can share an attestation under NDA, and recent pentest summary. We'll attach those to the security packet.
05:17 Marco Ruiz: Great. On timeline, we ideally want a pilot with three pilot customers by end of Q3. Is that feasible?
05:24 Jordan Hayes: It's tight but doable. We'll need the hardware spec sheet and sample workloads from you this week to scope the benchmark.
05:31 Ellen Cho: We'll push the spec and manifests.
05:34 Priya Menon: For the pilot we'll propose a simple benchmark: 1) baseline with fp16 model, 2) quantized 8-bit variant, 3) stress test for concurrent sessions. We'll measure p50/p95 and token cost.
05:48 Samir Patel: Who will run the initial benchmark? LodeCore or Redwood?
05:52 Jordan Hayes: Ideally jointly. Redwood can run tests on our sandbox and your engineers run the same reproducible test on hardware. We'll sync results.
06:00 Marco Ruiz: Anything else on technical blockers?
06:03 Rita Gomez: Just to re-iterate encryption at rest and KMS flow — we can't have keys leave our HSM.
06:09 Priya Menon: Understood. We'll confirm our HSM key wrapping flow.
06:14 Jordan Hayes: Ok let's do a quick recap. Action items: Jordan sends integration guide and security docs; Priya drafts benchmark plan; Ellen provides hardware specs and workloads; schedule pilot window late June. Any other items?
06:28 Ellen Cho: Can you also share a reference architecture diagram we can drop into our partner portal?
06:32 Aisha Khan: Yes we'll include a diagram and sample manifests.
06:35 Marco Ruiz: Good meeting. We'll expect the docs and then book the pilot.
06:39 Jordan Hayes: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by email with the packet and Slack channel invite.
06:44 Meeting ended.

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional mis-attributions (Speaker 2 noted as Jordan in some segments), background noise and brief crosstalk at 02:00-02:10. Proper nouns occasionally garbled (e.g., 'LodeCore' once transcribed as 'LoadCore'). References to artifacts: "partner-integration-onepager.pdf" (to be shared), "redwood-security-whitepaper.pdf", and a benchmark spreadsheet referenced as "LodeCore-Redwood-benchmark.xlsx".
